newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA DAMPEN PUSKAS' BIRTHDAY CELEBRATIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA DAMPEN PUSKAS' BIRTHDAY CELEBRATIONS.

text.p: Australia deflated the celebrations surrounding the 70th birthday of Ferenc Puskas when two goals in the last two minutes gave them a 3-1 win over Hungary in a friendly international on Wednesday.

The irony of Australia defeating Hungary in the week when the "Mighty Magyars" momentous 6-3 victory over England at Wembley in 1953 was back in the headlines, will not be lost on the soccer community.

The modern-day Hungary are a pale imitation of Puskas's great side of the 1950s and the old maestro was among the 18,000 crowd who watched in amazement as the team coached by Englishman Terry Venables scored twice in the closing stages to win.
Australia, on a tour of Europe as part of their warm-up for their World Cup qualifiers which start in June, took the lead in the sixth minute through Tony Vidmar who scored with a simple header.
The home side equalised through Laszlo Klausz who broke through the Australian defence in the 31st minute for a fine individual strike.

Second half pressure by Hungary failed to find a breakthrough and just as the match appeared to be ending in an honourable draw, goals in the 89th minute through Kevin Muscat and a second by Vidmar in the dying seconds gave Australia their victory.
